questions.question: Compression, tension and shearing are associated respectively with which plate boundaries?
Rock deep in the crust tends to FOLD rather than fault because:
options: It is always made of granite
Heat and confining pressure make it behave plastically, so it deforms without fracturing
There is no force acting at depth

questions.question: The correct order in which rock responds to increasing stress is:
options: Elastic deformation, plastic deformation, fracture and displacement

questions.question: Which condition makes fracturing (faulting) MORE likely than folding?
options: Very slow application of force over millions of years
Sudden application of force to cold, brittle surface rock

subtopics.title: Folds — Anticlines, Synclines and the Fold Family

questions.question: An anticline is:
options: A downfold, or trough, in the strata
An upfold, or arch, with limbs dipping away on both sides and the oldest rocks at its core
A fracture along which rock has moved
A block of crust dropped between two faults

questions.question: Arrange these folds in order of INCREASING compression:
Inversion of relief occurs because:
options: Synclines are always made of softer rock
Rivers only ever flow along anticlines
Rock stretched over an anticline crest cracks and erodes faster, while compressed syncline rock resists, so the arch may become a valley and the trough a ridge

questions.question: The sloping sides of a fold are called its:

subtopics.title: Faults and the Landforms They Make

questions.question: What distinguishes a fault from an ordinary crack or joint in rock?
options: Rock has actually MOVED along a fault
A fault is filled with lava
A fault occurs only in sedimentary rock

questions.question: In a NORMAL fault:
options: Compression drives the hanging wall up over the footwall
Movement is purely horizontal with no throw
Tension causes the hanging wall to slide DOWN relative to the footwall, leaving a fault scarp
Two plates slide past each other creating a trench

questions.question: A block of crust that DROPS between two parallel normal faults is called a:
options: Horst, seen as a block mountain
Graben, seen at the surface as a rift valley

questions.question: The vertical displacement along a fault plane is the throw. The horizontal displacement is the:

subtopics.title: The Cape Fold Mountains — and Describing Structures in Words

questions.question: The Cape Fold Mountains were formed:
options: By volcanic eruptions about 5 million years ago
By compression roughly 250 to 280 million years ago, while Gondwana was being assembled
By tension along the East African Rift
By glacial erosion during the last ice age

questions.question: The characteristic landscape pattern of the Cape Fold Mountains is:
options: Isolated flat-topped blocks with steep straight sides
Long, narrow, parallel ranges separated by long, narrow valleys
A staircase of step faults descending to the sea

questions.question: Why are the valleys between the Cape ranges so intensively farmed?
options: They are sheltered, have deep soils washed down from the ridges, and are watered by rivers rising in the mountains
They are the only flat land in South Africa
They receive no rainfall at all, which suits vines

questions.question: The recommended order for describing any structure in an answer is:
options: The force, the response of the rock, the shape produced, the resulting landform

subtopics.title: Push the Rug, Pull the Rug

questions.question: Pushing a rug across a floor until it rides up into ridges illustrates:
The chocolate comparison — sagging when pressed slowly, shattering when hit — illustrates that:
options: Rock type is the only thing that matters
The RATE at which force is applied helps decide whether rock bends or breaks

questions.question: Which rock is MOST likely to bend rather than snap?
options: Layered sandstone and shale deep in the crust

subtopics.title: Hills, Hollows and the Surprise Valley

questions.question: A syncline is best pictured as:
options: A trough or smile shape, with the layers sagging to a low point

questions.question: Bending a stack of newspaper cracks the OUTSIDE of the bend. In rock, this explains why:
options: Faults never form in folded rock
The crest of an anticline is stretched, cracked and attacked hardest by weathering and erosion
Folds cannot occur in sedimentary rock

questions.question: A fold that has been pushed over so far that it lies almost flat is called:
Inversion of relief means that in the finished landscape:
options: The anticline may form a valley and the syncline may stand up as a ridge
The rock layers turn upside down

questions.question: Standing on the floor of a rift valley, you would see:
options: A rounded, curved mountain crest on all sides
Flat ground in front of you with a long straight cliff wall on either side, and often a deep lake between them
A circular crater with a lava plug
A staircase of terraces climbing to a single summit

questions.question: A block mountain (horst) is recognised in the landscape by:
options: Curved, wavy crests running in parallel ranges
A cone shape with a crater at the summit
Steep straight sides and a flat top, as though cut with a knife

questions.question: Many parallel faults each dropping the land a little further produce:
options: Step faulting — a landscape descending like a staircase

questions.question: Driving from Worcester through the Hex River Valley — mountains left, mountains right, a fertile valley of vineyards between, repeating for a hundred kilometres — you are looking at:
options: Folding, from compression during the building of Gondwana
Step faulting along a transform boundary
